# Overview

This document summarizes the functions defined in [HoTTRijke/chapter5_eq.lean](../HoTTRijke/chapter5_eq.lean), in namespace `chapter5_myeq`.

The file introduces a custom identity type `MyEq`, proves basic equality properties, defines path composition operations, and develops transport and higher coherence constructions.

# Core Equality Type

## MyEq

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| MyEq.refl | `{α : Type} → (a : α) → MyEq a a` | Constructor witnessing reflexivity of equality. |

## Notation

| Notation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `a ≡ b` | Alias for `MyEq a b`. |
| `p • q` | Path concatenation via `concat_eq p q`. |

# Function Summary

## Equality Induction and Basic Laws

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| ind_eq | `{α : Type} → {a : α} → (P : (x : α) → (a ≡ x) → Type) → P a (MyEq.refl a) → ((x : α) → (p : a ≡ x) → P x p)` | Eliminator/induction principle for `MyEq`, reducing all equality proofs to reflexivity. |
| myEq_symm | `{α : Type} → {a x : α} → (a ≡ x) → (x ≡ a)` | Symmetry of equality (path inversion). |
| myEq_symm_refl | `{α : Type} → (a : α) → myEq_symm (MyEq.refl a) ≡ (MyEq.refl a)` | Shows symmetry preserves reflexivity. |
| myEq_refl | `{α : Type} → {a : α} → (a ≡ a)` | Reflexivity of equality. |
| myEq_trans | `{α : Type} → {a x y : α} → (a ≡ x) → (x ≡ y) → (a ≡ y)` | Transitivity of equality. |
| concat_eq | `{α : Type} → {x y z : α} → (x ≡ y) → (y ≡ z) → (x ≡ z)` | Equality concatenation (path composition), equivalent to transitivity. |
| concat_assoc | `{α : Type} → {a b c d : α} → (p : a ≡ b) → (q : b ≡ c) → (r : c ≡ d) → (p • (q • r)) ≡ ((p • q) • r)` | Associativity of path concatenation. |
| concat_right_unit | `{α : Type} → {a b : α} → (p : a ≡ b) → (p • (MyEq.refl b)) ≡ p` | Right identity law for concatenation. |
| concat_left_unit | `{α : Type} → {a b : α} → (p : a ≡ b) → ((MyEq.refl a) • p) ≡ p` | Left identity law for concatenation. |
| left_unit | `{α : Type} → {a b : α} → (p : a ≡ b) → (a ≡ b)` | Repackages left-unit composition as a term of the same equality type. |
| right_unit | `{α : Type} → {a b : α} → (p : a ≡ b) → (a ≡ b)` | Repackages right-unit composition as a term of the same equality type. |

## Action on Paths and Composition Properties

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| ap | `{α : Type} → {β : Type} → (f : α → β) → (x y : α) → (p : x ≡ y) → (f x ≡ f y)` | Applies a function to both sides of an equality (functorial action on paths). |
| sym_coctat_distributive | `{α : Type} → {x y z : α} → (p1 : x ≡ y) → (p2 : y ≡ z) → myEq_symm (p1 • p2) ≡ (myEq_symm p2) • (myEq_symm p1)` | Inversion distributes over concatenation in reverse order. (Name preserves a typo in the source — "coctat" for "concat".) |
| inv_con | `{α : Type} → {a b c : α} → (p : a ≡ b) → (q : b ≡ c) → (r : a ≡ c) → ((p • q) ≡ r) → (q ≡ (myEq_symm p • r))` | Solves for `q` from a composed path equation by composing with the inverse of `p`. |
| con_inv | `{α : Type} → {a b c : α} → (p : a ≡ b) → (q : b ≡ c) → (r : a ≡ c) → ((p • q) ≡ r) → (p ≡ r • (myEq_symm q))` | Solves for `p` from a composed path equation by composing with the inverse of `q`. |
| ap_id | `{α : Type} → (x y : α) → (p : x ≡ y) → p ≡ (ap (fun (x : α) => x) x y p)` | Shows `ap` on the identity function returns the same path. |
| ap_comp | `{α : Type} → {β : Type} → {γ : Type} → (f : α → β) → (g : β → γ) → (x y : α) → (p : x ≡ y) → ap g (f x) (f y) (ap f x y p) ≡ ap (g ∘ f) x y p` | Functoriality of `ap` with respect to composition. |

## Sigma Paths and Transport

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| unique_ref | `{α : Type} → (x y : α) → (p : x ≡ y) → (⟨x, MyEq.refl x⟩ : Σ (y' : α), x ≡ y') ≡ ⟨y, p⟩` | Uniqueness-style result for equality witnesses packaged in a sigma type. |
| transport | `{α : Type} → {x y : α} → (β : (x' : α) → Type) → (x ≡ y) → (β x → β y)` | Transports terms along equalities in dependent types. |
| lift_β | `(α : Type) → (β : (a : α) → Type) → (a x : α) → (b : β a) → (p : a ≡ x) → (⟨a, b⟩ : Σ a, β a) ≡ ⟨x, transport β p b⟩` | Lifts a base equality to an equality in a dependent pair (`Sigma`) via transport. |

## Higher Coherence

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| maclane_pentagon | `{α : Type} → (a b c d e : α) → (p : a ≡ b) → (q : b ≡ c) → (r : c ≡ d) → (s : d ≡ e) → Type` | **Currently a stub — see Possible Issues.** Intended to encode the Mac Lane pentagon coherence identity for associativity paths. |

# Typeclass Instance

| Name | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Trans instance for MyEq | `instance {α : Type} : Trans (@MyEq α) (@MyEq α) (@MyEq α)` | Registers transitivity so `Trans.trans` uses `myEq_trans`. |

# Possible Issues

1. **`maclane_pentagon` discards its own result.** The `by` block (`chapter5_eq.lean:173-207`)
   correctly builds five intermediate 2-paths `α₁`–`α₅` and then proves
   `have t : ((α₁ • α₂) • α₃) ≡ (α₄ • α₅) := by ...` — this `t` is exactly the pentagon
   coherence witness the exercise is supposed to produce. But the very last line of the block is
   `exact α`, which closes the goal (recall the def's return type is itself `Type`, since
   `maclane_pentagon` produces a *type*, not a proof) with the ambient carrier type `α` —
   completely ignoring `t`. As written, `maclane_pentagon a b c d e p q r s` reduces to just
   `α`, the original type, not to the pentagon-coherence type `((α₁ • α₂) • α₃) ≡ (α₄ • α₅)`.
   This looks like an unfinished definition — the likely fix is to end the block with
   `exact ((α₁ • α₂) • α₃) ≡ (α₄ • α₅)` (or simply return `t`'s type/proof, depending on whether
   the intent was to state the coherence as a `Type` or witness it as a term).
2. `sym_coctat_distributive` preserves a spelling typo from the source. It was previously spelled
   `sym_contat_distributive`; the source has since been renamed, but the new name is still a typo
   ("coctat" instead of "concat"). Documented as-is since it is a real declaration name that must
   be referenced verbatim.

# Notes

- The namespace is `chapter5_myeq` even though the file name is `chapter5_eq.lean`.
- The development follows Chapter 5 style HoTT path algebra: inversion, concatenation, action on paths (`ap`), and transport.
- This file is imported by `chapter5_ints.lean`, `chapter3_naturals_with_zero.lean`,
  `chapter5_props_naturals_with_zero.lean`, `Inductive_Int.lean`, `chapter6.lean`, and
  `chapter7.lean` — it is the most widely depended-on file in the project.
